newsitem.title: CHINA: SWIRE H1 PROPERTY PROFITS UP SHARPLY.
newsitem.headline: SWIRE H1 PROPERTY PROFITS UP SHARPLY.

text.p: Swire Pacific Ltd posted a sharp rise in property development sales in the first half of 1997 and said on Thursday it expected a further enhancement of property profits in the second half of the year.
Profit on the sale of development properties rose to HK$3.07 billion during the first six months of the year from HK$59 million in the same 1996 period.
Net rental income rose to HK$1.88 billion compared with HK$1.77 billion.

"The property division experienced further growth in rental income from its investment property portolio which was enhanced by significant profits from developments for sale arising in the main from further sales of residential units in the Island Place development," Swire Pacific said in a statement.
It said 315 residential units in Island Place, in North Point on Hong Kong Island, had been sold in the first half of 1997 "at appreciably higher prices than the 376 unit sales concluded in 1996".
The remaining 93 units at the development were expected to be sold in the second half of the year.
Swire Pacific said its Island Place office tower was completed last month and only two of the 25 floors remained unsold, while the adjacent shopping centre was almost fully let.

It said demand for its Floridian development on Hong Kong Island remained strong. Since June 30, 103 of the 214 completed residential units had been sold and the remaining 111 units were likely to be sold before the end of 1997.
The Hong Kong conglomerate also sold the 272-unit Courvoisier Courts rental apartment tower in Miami last month.
Swire Pacific said net rental income was expected to strengthen in the second half of 1997.

This was mainly due to a full contribution from reinstated areas of the Cityplaza shopping centre, as well as an initial contribution from the Cityplaza One office tower, due to be completed shortly. One third of Cityplaza One space was let.
"The property division expects further enhancement of profits in the second half-year as a result of sales of residential development properties and growth in net rental income," Swire Pacific said.
